Candidate-set objectives offer a stronger hypothesis than improving isolated margins. [SL@K (KDD 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05673) uses quantile-based truncation to target NDCG@K; relevant to top-10 selection, though its theory does not establish improvement on sampled HR@10. [DFTopK (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11472) provides a differentiable top-k operator with reported O(n) complexity, avoiding sorting and soft permutation matrices. Both suggest training-time alternatives for scores from one masked BERT4Rec; neither requires multiple predictors. Their published results do not establish effectiveness on this host benchmark.

False-negative robustness deserves a separate comparison. [PSL (2024 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00163) identifies exponential weighting in softmax as a source of false-negative sensitivity, replacing it with alternative activations and deriving tighter DCG surrogates under suitable choices. [Sampled-softmax analysis (TOIS 2024)](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) supports multi-negative competition and implicit hard-negative mining, making sampled cross-entropy a useful reference objective. These approaches operate on sampled scores without requiring differentiable sorting; aggressively emphasizing the hardest unobserved items can still amplify mislabeled negatives.

Practical experiment: keep the masked bidirectional backbone fixed and compare sampled cross-entropy, PSL, and a top-10 surrogate under matched candidate counts and compute. Exclude known training positives from negatives without consulting held-out labels. With nonuniform or in-batch sampling, [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) distinguishes the always-present positive from sampled negatives; sampling correction addresses a different issue from false-negative robustness. Select using unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10 and record GPU cost; margin improvements alone remain insufficient evidence.
